objective: Proof. (i) Balance: every 3-edge cut of a cubic incidence graph has a point side whose three ports are points and a line side whose three slots are lines. (ii) A composition across a cut fails iff the two sides' accepted relations are disjoint. (iii) A relation on k channels with full (k-1)-projections has at least 2^(k-1) states, with equality only for a parity coset; so two sides that both accept knots can fail together only as complementary parity cosets. (iv) Across every 3-edge cut of a knot's space the line side accepts exactly not-all-equal and the point side exactly equality (point lemma); double cuts give twelve-class knots, and joining two of them never fails. So the knot's spaces compose only through hubs, and a hub-free failing composition is parity. (v) The transpose of a knot's space is a knot's space and exchanges the two kinds of side.
status: Proved by KNOT-COMPOSE-20261101-001A-P001: every 3-edge cut of a cubic incidence graph is balanced (a point side with three ports, a line side with three slots); across every nontrivial 3-edge cut of a knot's space the line side accepts exactly not-all-equal and the point side exactly equality (point lemma), so the parts meet knot against hub; two sides that both accept knots fail together only as complementary parity cosets (an independent half of the cube is a colour class), and double cuts of knot's spaces give twelve-class knots that never fail together; so knot's spaces compose only through hubs and hub-free failure is parity; the transpose exchanges knot and hub sides
title: Knot's spaces compose only through hubs
